title: The last stanza
hookLine: sadaa sachidaanand: ever truth, consciousness and bliss, breaker of enemies, dwelling in all (Jaap 199)

lines: THE THEMES COME BACK AT THE END.
cards: Some music ends by coming home. The orchestra has wandered through storms and dances and quiet passages, and at the end, the themes from the opening come back, gathered up, all the instruments together, one last chord.
The music has arrived. Jaap Sahib ends in a similar way. It doesn't bring in a stranger in its last lines.
It gathers what it has said, and the languages it has said it in.

teach.b: Near the very end, back in the gliding bhujang prayat where the salutations began, comes this line: sadaa sachidaanand, satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda, samastul nivaasee. Take it slowly. Sadaa: always, ever.
Sachidaanand is three Sanskrit words fused: sat, truth or being; chit, consciousness; aanand, bliss. Ever truth, consciousness and bliss.
Satr pranaasee: the destroyer of enemies, the protector you met in the armed One and the breaker of the cruel. Then the language changes mid-line.
Kareemul kuninda: kareem is Arabic, the Generous; kuninda is Persian, the Maker. The generous Maker. And samastul nivaasee: the One who dwells in all, present in every land.

In one line, Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian sit side by side, the same mix the whole hymn has used: bliss, protection, generosity, presence everywhere, three weeks of themes gathered in one breath. That's the final chord.

teach.h: SADAA ANG SANGE: EVER BY YOUR SIDE.
teach.b: And the stanza that seals the hymn ends with sadaa ang sange: ever with you, by your side, close as your own limbs.
After stanza upon stanza of names too vast to picture, timeless, formless, king of kings, sun of suns, Jaap's last word isn't far away at all. It's right here.
Ever true, ever bliss, and ever beside you.

how: Sikhs end their morning recitation of Jaap Sahib with these closing stanzas, often reciting them from memory, before moving on to the Tav Prasad Savaiye.

o: truth, the one thing that is real

games.q: the last stanza — tap the pairs.

s: Jaap ends by introducing a brand-new idea
it gathers its themes and its languages into one final chord.
the closing line mixes Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian words
sachidaanand, kareem and kuninda sit side by side.
Jaap's last word puts the One far away
sadaa ang sange: ever beside you, close as your own limbs.

games.q: after stanza upon stanza of vast names, timeless, formless, king of kings, how does Jaap end?
o: with the One even farther away.
with the One ever beside you: sadaa ang sange.
with silence and no final line.
games.why: the vast One of every name turns out, in the last line, to be close as your own limbs.

practice: Say the last line aloud twice, slowly, in the snake's rhythm: sadaa sachidaanand, satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda, samastul nivaasee.
Then say the sealing words once, gently, sadaa ang sange, with a hand on your arm or over your heart, and feel how close that is. Sit with the closeness.

wordCard.voice: Sadaa. Always, ever — it opens Jaap's final chord: ever truth, consciousness and bliss, the generous Maker dwelling in all, and ever by your side.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sadaa, always, ever; it opens sadaa sachidaanand and sadaa ang sange.

carryVoice: Your line: ever true, ever bliss. Sadaa ang sange: ever by your side. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Jaap Sahib, closing stanzas (198–199): sadaa sachidaanand satr pranaasee, kareemul kuninda samastul nivaasee; sadaa ang sange
